rv.q: Not since Felix Ungar and Oscar Madison moved in together has Broadway had such an odd couple on the boards.
Seen side by side, in a production that brings to mind a desperately assembled television variety show from the 1970s, these two headliners clash like polka dots paired with plaid.
The show then ends with a Merman-Martin-like medley that has propulsion but no pizzazz — a reflection of much of All About Me‘s fair-to-middlin’ quality.
It's just this kind of recycled material that makes "All About Me" all about meh.
Such antics are supposed to be frantic, unpredictable, and delightful - they never quite seem to be any of the three.

cn.t: This mismatched pairing of Dame Edna and Michael Feinstein in a musty variety show format fails to satisfy, with critics finding the odd couple lacks chemistry and leaves fans wanting more of each performer separately.

vs.sum: A Roundabout Theatre Company house with excellent sightlines and good sound. Post-renovation seating is comfortable with decent legroom. Standout facilities include 30 women's restroom stalls — triple the building code requirement — virtually eliminating intermission lines.

acc.note: Elevator to all levels. 3 hearing loops. 100 Sennheiser hearing devices. 12 wheelchair seats.
